newsitem.title: USA: U.S.-Japan film dispute to linger, Mondale says.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Japan film dispute to linger, Mondale says.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador to Japan Walter Mondale said on Thursday he did not expect a dispute with Japan over the color film market to be resolved before April, when a World Trade Organization panel is likely to rule on the issue.

Mondale, speaking to reporters before addressing a wood-industry conference, said trade relations between the two allies generally had been improving despite thorny disputes over color film, insurance and civil aviation.
"We've made good progress in trade -- the data show that," he said.

For example, he said the U.S. wood-products industry is "on the verge of a major breakthrough" in the Japanese market. Earlier a Clinton administration official said U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky likely would back an industry recommendation to remove Japan from a trade watch list for wood products.
Barshefsky this month asked WTO panels to rule on a dispute between Eastman Kodak Co. and Fuji Photo Film Co. Ltd. after the two nations were unable to resolve the issue through consultations.
Mondale said in response to a question that he expected the dispute settlement panels to come to their decision in April, and he said he did not hold out hope of an earlier settlement.
Kodak argues that it has lost $5.5 billion in potential trade over the past few years because of restrictive practices favoring Fuji, which holds 70 percent of the Japanese market.
